children: saw its trading volume crater by almost 50% in quiet weekend trading even as the broader crypto market continued to face selling pressure.

Dogecoin trading volume fell 49% in the past 24 hours to $607 million, data from CoinMarketCap showed, suggesting less market activity around the popular dog coin as traders evaluate conditions amid the ongoing market sell-off.
Lower trading volume might suggest a temporary slowdown in participation, particularly during weekends when activity across digital asset markets may ease.
Dogecoin fell for the fourth day on Saturday as investors weighed hotter-than-expected inflation data and Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's latest comments on interest rates.

The inflation data comes two weeks ahead of the next interest rate decision, with Fed Chairman Warsh on Thursday declining to offer any signals as to whether there will be another interest rate hike this month.

Dogecoin began to decline broadly from a high of $0.097 on October 4, 2026, with the drop causing it to fall below its 50 and 200 daily moving averages. As selling progressed, the daily RSI approached the oversold area and is now at 34.

If the Dogecoin price rebounds, the $0.081 level remains one to watch, with so many tokens changing hands at this price. The URPD data shows about 36 billion DOGE were previously traded around $0.081.
Whales appear to be buying near $0.081, as since October 12, large holders have reportedly added about 600 million DOGE.
Support is expected in the $0.07 range if the price declines further.

title: Dogecoin Volume Drops 50% in Quiet Weekend Trade Amid Market Selloff
